title: RefCell Guard Lifetime in Let Bindings
prompt: How does assigning a RefCell borrow to a named variable differ from calling a method on it in a single statement?
answer: A named variable keeps the Ref or RefMut guard alive until the end of its enclosing block. A single-statement call like cell.borrow().len() drops the guard at the semicolon. Holding named guards too long is the primary cause of RefCell panics.
